statement: Theorem 2.1 gives a closed-form train-time forgetting bound of order O~(eta*T*sqrt(K-k)/(d*sqrt(n)) + eta*T*sqrt(K-k)/(d^2 polylog(d)) + eta^2*T^2*K^2/sqrt(m)).
source: Theorem 2.1 (Thm 2.1), Eq. (4), arXiv:2510.05573v2; kernel-regime forgetting object Eq. after Thm 2.2.

mutation_test.description: Break the orthogonality assumption between task means (random near-parallel directions instead of mutually orthogonal ones).
mutation_test.note: Non-orthogonal tasks introduce a constant cross-task interference bias in x_k^T A_j x_k that does NOT vanish as n grows, so the clean closed-form bound (which relies on orthogonal clusters) no longer describes the data and forgetting fails to vanish.
